titulo: Does hot water wash your hands cleaner? (CDC: temperature doesn't matter; soap and 20 seconds do)
receta: error cotidiano con regla para guardar (pasos y 20 segundos) + pregunta de una palabra
destinatario: Se lo manda alguien que se lava las manos con agua fría a su amigo que cree que hay que hacerlo con agua hirviendo.

interaccion.guardar: Wet, soap, scrub for 20 seconds, rinse, dry. Water temperature doesn't matter.
interaccion.comentar: What song do you hum to time twenty seconds?

fuentes: CDC, Handwashing: Clean Hands Save Lives (water temperature, 20 seconds, five steps)
Jensen et al., Rutgers University, Journal of Food Protection, 2017

frases.texto: You crank the water to hot so it kills the germs on your hands.

frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The CDC says the temperature of the water doesn't change how many germs come off.
A Rutgers study in twenty seventeen tested water from sixty to one hundred degrees. No meaningful difference in germ removal.
What does the work is soap and scrubbing. Wet, soap, scrub for twenty seconds, rinse, dry.
Heads up: hotter water can irritate your skin, so use whatever feels comfortable.
Save this for the next time you're at the sink.
So what song do you hum to time twenty seconds?
Send this to the friend who rinses for two seconds and calls it clean.
